summary: Requirement R1.1 says 3 weeks or less, the final report sets 3–4 weeks, and nothing links them.
Three estimates of audit queue time (2–3, 3–4 and 6–8 days), nobody measured it.

x.answer: Three people gave different estimates and nobody measured it, so there is no single binding value.

summary: Earlier sources give about six weeks while the interim estimate gave 6.5-7 weeks; the final 6-6.5 weeks sits alongside the exact-six-week statements without resolving them.
The project brief says ClearPath has 78 employees, while the kickoff meeting says about 120 people, and nothing indicates which figure prevails.
The board presentation is given as November 20 (meetings), December 10 (client emails), and November 28 (internal email), with nothing resolving which one prevails.
Sources disagree on the number of team leaders: four (Priya's interview, meeting-002, Marcus in meeting-003) versus six (Thomas's brief, observation-005), with no document settling which prevails.

Reported IT provisioning time varies: 2-3 business days (Michele), 3-5 days (Priya, David), a week or more (Priya), and 3-7 days (final presentation), with nothing establishing which is authoritative.
The SOW commits to 15-20 interviews, but the interviews proposed, scheduled and conducted number only six.
The SOW plans 8-12 observation sessions, but completion is reported only as a three-week observation period with no session count.
The SOW excludes implementation as a separate engagement, while later communications plan an intake automation start and an implementation kickoff in January without saying whether scope changed.
The process map estimates total cycle time of 8-15 weeks, while the final report gives an average of 5-8 days.
Marco's self-report says 5 active clients while Priya's ops records and the observation show 3, and nothing says which prevails.
Phase One discovery was planned as 2-3 weeks from September 15, but the observations phase only closes on October 31, about 6.5 weeks later.
Internal notes attribute the audit delay to data availability from ClearPath, while the external email attributes it to data compilation taking longer than anticipated.
Marcus describes the project as tighter than ideal at week 6, while the later external message claims it is on track for all December 1 commitments.
Final delivery is given as Nov 28, December 1, and December 2 (Friday) with nothing saying which prevails.
Written report due Nov 10 conflicts with interim reports due Nov 15 or Nov 25, and nothing resolves which applies.
The kickoff meeting says the Milan team is mostly client-facing, while the emails say its 8 people are mostly administrative with light compliance work.
Docure Consulting is described as recently acquired by ComplianceCare BV and also as an acquisition target in the same document.
Marco reports usually 4 or 5 audits waiting for review, while a later meeting reports average queues of fifteen to twenty items before senior review, and nothing says which prevails.
An earlier peer-review pilot was abandoned for lack of trust in peer review, yet the roadmap later requires peer review before client delivery.
